title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether integrating a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier with a bounded automated repair budget increases the fraction of intent‑driven network‑change proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001; preregistration SHA‑256 = 425cb1652354120cf48f686b964723d64c76d0a8abe53cd5b5ad0eaa1af71fc7) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic semantic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Each paired intent produced one shared_initial generation that was evaluated under two conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (deterministic validation and ≤1 automated repair). Outcomes: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and the one‑repair budget, the single‑shot generator was near ceiling, limiting observable deterministic rescue. We archive preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts and interpret results with respect to estimand conditioning, validator coverage, repair budget, and operational deployment policies.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, template synthesis, and automated repair. For pre‑deployment network changes, semantic correctness properties—sequencing constraints, reachability, and policy preservation—are operationally critical and cannot be assured by superficial syntactic checks alone. A common engineering pattern couples generative models with deterministic validators and bounded automated repair (generate→validate→repair) to reduce operational risk. However, the measurable benefit of such guarded pipelines depends on what is held fixed (the estimand), the single‑shot quality of the generator, the validator’s expressiveness, and the permitted repair budget.

We preregistered a paired experiment (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) to quantify the deterministic rescue achievable when the same single LLM candidate is evaluated under two treatments. For each intent the pipeline produced exactly one shared_initial candidate using the declared generator (gpt-5-mini) and compared: (a) baseline—accept the single candidate without repair, and (b) guarded—run a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and allow at most one automated repair which itself is re‑validated. The primary research question: does adding a deterministic verifier plus at most one automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting that same candidate without repair?

Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation isolating deterministic rescue under a shared_initial estimand; (2) a complete execution and analysis bundle including validator traces and the single automated repair transcript; and (3) an evidence‑grounded interpretation of estimand conditioning, ceiling effects, and operational implications for NetOps pipelines.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and system papers document LLM applications to NetOps tasks (intent translation, template synthesis, protocol test generation, and repair) and emphasize engineering tradeoffs when combining generation with deterministic checks and tools [1–4]. Planner‑centric and ReAct‑style architectures enable LLMs to call external validators and orchestrate multi‑step workflows; these tool‑augmentation designs motivate measuring how much correctness is attributable to the validator or to additional model calls/resampling [5,6]. Empirical reports show that generate→validate→repair scaffolds often improve surface correctness metrics relative to unconstrained generation, but the effect size depends on validator coverage and whether evaluations permit resampling or iterative regeneration [3,4].

Methodological gaps in the literature motivated our design. First, prior evaluations often conflate verifier benefits with resampling or verifier‑guided regeneration; isolating deterministic rescue requires conditioning on a single shared generator draw per intent. Second, publicly available NetOps benchmarks frequently emphasize syntactic correctness rather than semantically rich invariants (reachability, sequencing, policy preservation); evaluations tied to expressive validators are necessary to assess operational safety [2,3]. Hybrid approaches that combine symbolic fault localization or formal checks with generative repair report variable success across fault classes, underscoring that validator expressiveness and permitted edit operators determine practical value [7,8].
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The confirmatory design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) was preregistered and archived (preregistration SHA‑256 = 425cb1652354120cf48f686b964723d64c76d0a8abe53cd5b5ad0eaa1af71fc7). The primary estimand is the absolute paired difference in the unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded − baseline) computed on N = 300 paired intents after prespecified inclusion/exclusion rules. The preregistration fixed the analysis executor, multiplicity plan, and the bounded repair budget (≤1 automated repair).

Task generation and stratification. A deterministic task generator produced a synthetic_topology_suite stratified into three difficulty strata (low/medium/high). Each manifest entry encodes the natural‑language intent, initial and expected final states, sequencing invariants (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), preserve_unspecified_state constraints, and protected_interfaces. The confirmatory run sampled 100 pairs per stratum (N = 300 total).

Shared_initial generation and model configuration. To isolate deterministic verifier/repair rescue from resampling effects we implemented the shared_initial estimand: for each pair a single shared_initial candidate was produced and reused verbatim for both baseline and guarded conditions. The declared generator was gpt-5-mini (requested_model = "gpt-5-mini"); the guarded condition ran deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and, if flagged, permitted at most one constrained automated repair edit.

Validator and repair operator. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performs deterministic checks of sequencing invariants, required_command_count, preservation-of-state invariants, and forbidden‑template protections. Scoring is binary: unflagged candidate = pass. The automated repair operator is a constrained edit routine limited to localized sequencing and insertion edits (e.g., inserting a missing 'admin down' before a VLAN/MTU change). Repairs are applied only when the validator flags the shared_initial candidate and are re‑validated deterministically.

Missingness, contamination, and stopping rules. The preregistration defined exclusion rules (pairs excluded only if both calls failed due to provider outage) and included negative controls and contamination checks. The confirmatory stopping rule required halting if >20% of attempted pairs were excluded for dual‑call outages; this did not occur in the main run.

Analysis. The preregistered analysis executor computed the paired contingency (n11,n10,n01,n00), the absolute paired difference, an exact two‑sided McNemar test, and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). The pilot described in the preregistration for discordance estimation was not executed prior to the main run and no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed; this omission and its implications are reported in Results and Discussion.

Reproducibility. All design artifacts (preregistration, task manifests, model configuration, validator and repair traces, execution logs, and analysis inputs) are archived in the run bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement to permit deterministic replay of the confirmatory executor.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The confirmatory run produced completed_episode_count = 600 yielding complete_pair_count = 300 paired observations under the shared_initial protocol. Model call accounting: model_calls_used = 301 (300 shared_initial generations + 1 repair invocation). No pairs were excluded and no provider/infrastructure dual‑call outages occurred.

Primary outcomes. Binary scoring produced baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300 (baseline = 299/300 = 0.9966667; guarded = 300/300 = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test (operating on n10 and n01) returned p = 1.0. The absolute paired improvement (guarded − baseline) equals 0.0033333. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729, B = 10000) is [0.00, 0.01]. Because discordance is minimal (m = n10 + n01 = 1), standard exact inference has limited sensitivity; the bootstrap CI provides a complementary effect‑size bound.

Per‑stratum diagnostics. Stratified tallies were: low difficulty baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; medium baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; high baseline = 99/100 and guarded = 100/100. The sole discordant pair occurred in the high stratum.

Repair diagnostic. The single discordant pair invoked the permitted automated repair. Validator traces attribute the initial failure to a sequencing omission (a required 'admin down' missing before a VLAN/MTU change). The constrained repair inserted the missing sequencing command; after this single localized edit the deterministic validator reported valid == true and the guarded condition counted a pass. The repair therefore produced a deterministic rescue with one additional repair invocation in the confirmatory run.

Contamination and missingness. Contamination checks found no unexpected passes on negative controls and the missingness summary reports zero failed or unscorable episodes and zero excluded pairs under the preregistered rules.

Operational footprint. The guarded pipeline incurred one additional repair stage call across 300 pairs (model_calls_used = 301), indicating minimal marginal model‑call cost for deterministic rescue under the chosen repair budget and operator on this synthetic suite.
sections.discussion:
Estimand and operational alignment. Conditioning on a single LLM draw per intent (shared_initial) corresponds to operational policies that constrain model calls for cost, latency, or governance reasons. Under such policies the guarded pipeline measures only deterministic validator and bounded repair rescue applied to the same candidate. Workflows that permit resampling, verifier‑guided generation, or interactive steering change the estimand and typically increase achievable success rates by exploiting generator variance; such workflows should be evaluated under different preregistered estimands.

Ceiling effects and pilot omission. Baseline single‑shot performance was near ceiling (299/300) on this synthetic suite, producing minimal discordance (m = 1) and limited power to detect small absolute improvements. The preregistered pilot intended to estimate discordance was not executed; had it been run it likely would have revealed higher baseline quality and motivated design choices (e.g., different task sampling, larger sample, or alternative estimand) to increase inferential sensitivity.

Validator coverage and failure‑mode dependence. The observed failure mode was a sequencing omission; other classes (reachability violations, ACL semantics) were not prevalent in this synthetic distribution. Guarded pipeline utility depends on the deployment distribution of failure modes and on validator expressiveness. Richer validators that detect reachability and policy semantics would likely increase observed rescue potential; conversely, operator policies that disallow automated edits limit guarded pipelines to detection and human escalation.

Repair budget tradeoffs. We intentionally limited automated repair to a single constrained edit to bound deterministic rescue and measure minimal automated intervention. Iterative repair, larger edit operators, or verifier‑guided regeneration would constitute different estimands and could materially increase rescue rates at the cost of additional model calls and design complexity.

Practical implications. For organizations that tightly budget model calls, the shared_initial estimand provides an operationally meaningful upper bound for deterministic verifier/repair rescue applied to one candidate. In this run, bounded repair produced a single deterministic rescue at negligible extra model‑call cost; in deployments with different task distributions or weaker generators the guarded pipeline may deliver larger absolute benefits.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired comparison (N = 300) using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 under a shared_initial estimand, baseline single‑shot generation produced 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300, yielding an absolute paired improvement of 0.00333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). A single constrained automated repair produced the lone deterministic rescue. The near‑ceiling baseline limits inferential sensitivity for small absolute improvements under the shared_initial estimand; follow‑up studies should vary estimand conditioning, task distributions, model strength, and repair budgets to map operational tradeoffs more broadly.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre‑specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation).
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
